reason: Asthma is an immune-mediated airway disease; pulmonary and infectious_immune are appropriate primary axes. Intermittent severity adds no organ.
Developmental impairment supports neurologic involvement as the defining axis. Sparse evidence warrants low confidence and does not establish additional common organ damage.

Skeletal myopathy and cardiomyopathy define this desmin disorder. Respiratory insufficiency arises from skeletal muscle weakness, without demonstrated pulmonary damage; the nervous-system ancestor does not establish neural disease.
Orofacial clefting directly affects the mouth, covered by gastrointestinal. The facial-skeleton ancestor alone does not require an additional musculoskeletal label.

Bone fragility and craniosynostosis define the skeletal disease. Hydrocephalus in 2/2 and dentinogenesis imperfecta in 1/2 support neurologic and gastrointestinal involvement; proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.

External auditory canal atresia and conductive hearing impairment define an otologic disorder. The broad otorhinolaryngologic parent does not establish airway disease; hyposmia lacks a qualifying frequency.

Intellectual disability and eczema define the syndrome. Thumb hypoplasia at 80–99% and palatal cleft at 30–79% support musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal involvement. Eyelid narrowing alone does not establish functional damage.

The tumour originates in the liver and consists of malignant lymphoid cells, supporting hepatic, haematologic and infectious_immune primary axes. Its gastrointestinal-lymphoma parent does not imply bowel involvement.

Erythroid/myeloid hypoplasia and combined immunodeficiency support haematologic and infectious_immune primary axes. The supplied evidence does not establish common hearing damage in this specific phenotype.
Toxic myocarditis directly damages the myocardium. A toxic cause does not itself establish infection, autoimmunity or another immune-mediated mechanism, so cardiovascular alone is appropriate.
